Alex: Quick sync — proposing an 'atomic slab' carve for session handling next quarter. Need to align on slab size, migration windows, rollback gates.
Marcus: +1 on smaller slabs — 1wk slabs limit blast radius and make rollbacks easier.
Jess: Agree smaller, but we need explicit SLI gates before each ramp (tail latency, error rate, 95/99 p99).
Sophia: Also: where does KV ownership land? runtime cache vs session-service durable store?
Marcus: My vote: runtime keeps hot in-memory cache for reads; session-service owns durable writes/primary store.
Alex: Proposed pattern: thin runtime adapter for writes that proxies to session-service; reads first try runtime cache then forward. Dual-write during migration window.
Jess: Can we gate cache invalidation behavior via feature flag (strict vs best-effort)? We don't want stale tokens causing auth failures.
Sophia: Yes, but must add metrics: per-tenant cache hit/miss, tail latency, consistency errors.
Alex: Migration plan sketch: 1) deploy adapter in read-forward mode, 2) dual-write to session-service for new slabs, 3) start canary at 1% traffic for one slab, 4) monitor SLIs, ramp to 20/50/100%. Rollback by disabling adapter flag and draining.
Marcus: Rollback checklist: traffic split back, disable adapter feature flag, sweep inconsistent records via backfill job. Estimate backfill time = ~2h per 10M sessions.
Jess: Test plan: integration harness + replay captured production traces against canary. Who owns traces and redaction?
Sophia: Platform owns sampling/redaction. I'll file INFRA-6421 to add a replay pipeline and tag traces for this migration.
Alex: I'll draft a short RFC with sequence diagrams and failure modes. Assign code owners for runtime adapter and session-store backfill.
Jess: One more: load on session-service during ramp — add autoscale policy and throttles. Also add request hedging for p95 spikes.
Marcus: For slab size: 1wk default but allow tenant-specific override; we'll need migration tooling to join/split slabs.
Alex: CLI for canary split we can run: 
```sh
redwood traffic split --service session-service --from runtime --percent 1
```
Sophia: Nice. Also add a safety guard: automatic rollback if p99 latency increases >30% for >5m.
deploy-bot: Deployment trigger received for branch feature/atomic-slab-adapter — staging roll started.
Alex: Thanks — timeline target: RFC by Friday, infra ticket linked, small spike next sprint. Can everyone reply with LGTM or blockers by EOD?
